class_id: an ISO string bound where the ORM expects a Date, following a raw-SQL rule on an ORM path
feature: every drizzle query that compares or writes a `timestamp()` column through the query builder (eq/gt/gte/lt/lte/between, .set(), .values(), onConflictDoUpdate) in web/ and packages/shared/
symptom: the project's IST rule says to bind `date.toISOString()` (a string), never a Date object, to a naive timestamp column. That is right for raw node-postgres parameters, where a Date is serialised in the process's LOCAL zone. It is wrong on the drizzle path: drizzle's PgTimestamp.mapToDriverValue calls `value.toISOString()` on whatever it receives, so a string throws `TypeError: value.toISOString is not a function`. The error is wrapped (DatabaseError -> NonRetryableError) and, with a logger that drops `cause`, surfaces only as a generic 500. Wider shape: a rule written for one binding layer, applied to a layer with the opposite contract, turns a timezone guard into a crash.
first_seen: 2026-09-25 -- IPODhan. (1) /api/ipos/[slug]/demand-graph returned HTTP 500 for every IPO with demand data (prod floor e_route_sweep: prasol-chemicals 09-16, lcc-projects 09-17, veegaland-developers 09-20, jindal-supreme 09-23; issue #954). Reproduced on ipodhan_test by the #954 builder: `TypeError: value.toISOString is not a function` at PgTimestamp.mapToDriverValue from the demand-graph repository query; fixed in PR #1069. (2) The #1033 builder's first fix attempt bound `.toISOString()` into drizzle `.set()` and crashed the same way (caught by its real-function round trip before commit; PR #1067 kept Date objects).
fix_prs: #1069 MERGED e555855b (demand-graph query binds a Date; web logger keeps the wrapped cause); #1067 MERGED 45a27884 (corrigendum accept keeps Date objects). Rule wording correction (.claude/rules/ist-timezone.md: 'bind toISOString()' applies to raw pg parameters only; drizzle-mapped timestamp() columns take a Date) was owner-approved 2026-09-25 (Q4) and lands with the detection check in PR #1079. Related: web logger has no redaction (#1073).
detection_check: scripts/ci/check-drizzle-iso-string.mjs (PR gate `gate` job, .github/workflows/pr-gate.yml), registry entry docs/reviews/detection-checks/iso_string_bound_to_drizzle_timestamp.json. Classifies every schema column by JS property name (default-mode timestamp() = flaggable; timestamp(mode:'string') and date() = exempt; a name declared both ways anywhere is ambiguous and skipped, favouring a false negative over blocking legitimate code), strips sql`` template bodies (the raw-pg path, where .toISOString() stays correct), then flags .toISOString() bound to a drizzle comparison operator (eq/ne/gt/gte/lt/lte/between/inArray/notInArray) or a .set()/.values() field on a flaggable column. Zero live offenders on the current tree (verified 2026-09-25); baseline file scripts/ci/drizzle-iso-string-baseline.json is empty and may only shrink. Self-test scripts/tests/check-drizzle-iso-string.test.mjs is red on a planted gte(ipos.createdAt, d.toISOString()) and green on gte(ipos.createdAt, d) and sql`${d.toISOString()}`. Also flags shape 2: any `sql<Date>` type argument outside comments (raw sql results are never mapped, so the value is text; the real #954 line, ipo-repository.ts:1680 at e555855b^, makes the check exit 1). Known gap: columns are classified by JS property name across the whole schema, not per table, so a bad bind on a column whose name is ALSO declared as date() or mode:'string' on another table passes silently.
